note: All three layers evaluated under the identical protocol on the same held-out test set.
finding: The two-stage model (ALS retrieve + LightGBM rerank) beats the popularity baseline on every accuracy metric: Recall@10 +13.5% (0.964% vs 0.849%), Recall@20 +19.3%, and NDCG@10 +37.5% (0.618% vs 0.449%). It also nearly triples the baseline's catalog coverage (2.41% vs 0.0077%) while ALS alone had lost badly on accuracy (roughly 10x worse than the baseline) despite reaching more of the catalog. The reranker appears to recover ALS's broader candidate pool while using popularity, recency, and category-affinity features to correct for ALS's weak personalization signal on this very sparse dataset (median 1 training event per user). This is the headline result of the project: naive collaborative filtering alone does not beat a well-chosen popularity baseline here, but combining it with explicit features in a learned reranker does, modestly but genuinely.
